scope: Calculated estimates, not observed match timings or win rates. Neutral civilization, no upgrades unless stated; continuous work and no combat. Live inputs are hashed below.

renewable_gold_demand.scope: A chosen replacement rate, not measured AI production. Sacred income can cover this for its controller; the opponent must mine or trade.

expansion.tradeoff: Spends wood/gold before Castle and food on workers before troops. Four extra workers occupy eight population. Gains a drop-off and production queue; needs protected work and continual food funding.

wheelbarrow.haul_assumption: 120 world units each way at60 units/s, carry30, food/wood, no crowding or idle time
wheelbarrow.scope: Illustrative steady-state throughput, not an immediate25% increase in delivered resources.

openings.name: Early aggression
openings.benefit: Can pressure exposed workers before opponents finish Feudal investment
openings.cost: Food competes with new workers; Warriors are slow and vulnerable to bows and Town Center fire

openings.name: Feudal pressure
openings.investment: Archery Range or Stable, mixed food/wood/gold army
openings.benefit: Counters enemy composition and contests mines/Sacred without Castle expense
openings.cost: Recurring gold demand and delayed siege; poor unsupported attacks into towers

openings.name: Defensive economy
openings.investment: Workers, Wheelbarrow, farms and selective tower coverage
openings.benefit: Renewable food and efficient protected production
openings.cost: Static defenses cannot defend every mine or caravan; gives the opponent map control

openings.name: Two Town Centers
openings.investment: Feudal expansion plus paid worker queues
openings.benefit: Faster workforce growth and another resource drop-off
openings.cost: 400W100G plus worker food delays army/Castle; extra workers must survive to repay investment

openings.name: Castle priority
openings.investment: 800F400G after Feudal, then Workshop and Siege
openings.benefit: Long-range building pressure can break entrenched defenses
openings.cost: Age adds no free HP/attack scaling; siege needs escorts and is vulnerable to flanks

civilizations.name: French
civilizations.strength: Full-strength buildings and160HP Horsemen; balanced unit roster
civilizations.tradeoff: No gathering specialization or ranged reach bonus
civilizations.strategy_fit: Flexible counter army, defended expansion, escorted Castle siege

civilizations.name: English
civilizations.tradeoff: 60HP Longbows and130HP Horsemen; recurring gold still needed
civilizations.strategy_fit: Protected bows, wood-funded expansion and farms; vulnerable to close flanks

civilizations.name: Mongols
civilizations.strategy_fit: Fast food-funded recruitment, raids or faster worker growth; exposed expansions require mobile defense

limits: No opening is claimed equally strong from calculations alone. Seed/civilization simulations and hands-on checks are recorded separately.
Finite map stocks and per-civilization villager gathering rates are unchanged. No resource silently expires.
Standard Sacred hold changes360 to300 seconds only for new matches; actual endings still depend on capture, contest and defending fighters.
